title: Broader systemic changes needed to prevent more deaths in custody: PAGC
subtitle: In a separate statement the FSIN expressed support for the family of Saul Laliberte, who died in Prince Albert police custody in November 2021.
article: The Prince Albert Grand Council says it's dedicated to working with the Prince Albert Police Service to achieve necessary reforms after the force announced one of its officers has been charged in connection with a 33-year-old man's 2021 death in custody.

Saul Laliberte died after he was taken to the police's detention centre on Nov. 7, 2021 . Last week, Prince Albert police said a 21-year member of the force has been charged with criminal negligence causing death and failure to provide the necessities of life. Following an investigation by Saskatoon police into Laliberte's death, the Crown recommended charges be laid.
Court records obtained by the StarPhoenix identify the officer as Tyson Morash, 50. The charges were laid by Saskatoon police on June 21.
Morash has been relieved of active duty, pending the outcome of court proceedings. He is scheduled to appear in Prince Albert provincial court on July 25.
PAGC Grand Chief Brian Hardlotte, in a statement issued Friday, commended the Prince Albert police for making this decision to relieve Morash of active duty.
"This action demonstrates their dedication to maintaining public trust and ensuring an impartial and fair investigation," Hardlotte said.

But the PAGC said that, given the series of deaths in Prince Albert police custody in 2021, it is emphasizing the "urgent need" for a "thorough, unbiased review of PAPS's procedures, standards, and practices."
Hardlotte said he's committed to a collaborative approach with the police force and others for a more inclusive and equitable system.

"These changes must make sure everyone is included and treated fairly, and that the safety and well-being of everyone in our community is put first," Hardlotte said of the reforms PAGC is calling for.
In a statement issued on Thursday, the Federation of Sovereign Indigenous Nations expressed support for Laliberte's family and said interim Police Chief Patrick Nogier "took action quickly."

"However, our concerns involve tragic deaths of First Nations in the care of the (p)olice service; these events are examples of systemic racism; there is no room for any public institution that risks managing the safety of any person; this includes the responsibility of Health and their acceptance to risk manage the safety of vulnerable people who are in police custody," the FSIN said.
The FSIN said the Laliberte family is requesting privacy.

Laliberte was the third person in fewer than 30 days in the fall of 2021 to die while in custody of Prince Albert police. He had been taken to police detention on Nov. 7, 2021 after his arrest and was found unresponsive in the detention cell a few hours later. In-detention paramedics attempted to revive him and he was taken to Victoria Hospital, where he died.
The province assigned an independent observer to all three investigations, while the coroner conducted separate investigations.
The PAGC and FSIN called on the Saskatchewan government to intervene following the deaths.

In November 2022, the province called an independent review to be led by former Edmonton police chief Rod Knecht , which focused on the Prince Albert Police Service's operations. The review has not yet been publicly released.

In an interview with the StarPhoenix Wednesday, Nogier said the deaths led to an internal review of the force's policy and protocols, which are related to detention audits being conducted - but not yet completed - by the province.
Prince Albert police made changes at their detention facility, including ensuring there are more robust checks and implementing an improved screening process.

"While we appreciate the efforts to improve detention facilities, we must not lose sight of the broader, more complex systemic changes needed to prevent such tragedies from happening again," Hardlotte said in the statement.

"We plan on closely monitoring the findings of the independent review led by former Edmonton Police Chief Rod Knecht, and we strongly urge for the prompt release of the report to ensure transparency and clarity for Saul Laliberte's family and our larger community."
